ownership_reason: Only the gold decides the external attribute word of the entry: the Unix permissions in the upper sixteen bits and the low byte (a read-only mark when the owner-write bit is clear, the directory attribute 0x10 for a directory entry). Hops 1-4 pass the entry and the mode along unchanged and the facade only writes the platform; any change of the mode above the gold also changes the upper sixteen bits, which the trigger checks. The gold's javadoc promises the attributes 'in a way that is understood by Info-Zip's unzip command', in which a directory entry carries the MS-DOS directory attribute in the low byte; the variant writes 0 there for 'foo/'. The convention that an entry's stored attributes mark it as a directory is pinned outside the gold: AsiExtraField.getMode(int) gives a directory entry's stored mode the directory type DIR_FLAG ('the file mode for given permissions with the correct file type'), ZipArchiveEntry.isDirectory defines a directory entry (a name ending in '/') and ZipArchiveEntry.getUnixMode reads the permissions back from the upper sixteen bits; AsiExtraFieldTest::testModes and ::testReparse pass, and the trigger's file-entry assertions hold.
